content: Hi. I'm giving a couple of lean talks to tech people in the near future and I think my audience would be far more interested in what's going on in the wider ecosystem rather than just hearing me going on about mathematics. What's the current state of the Signal Shot project?

Hi Kevin! We were just discussing in the last weeks how we need to figure out a way to better communicate the current status! Work is actively proceeding on many fronts and so organised is various distinct subprojects. No substantial blockers but something could be said about how certain things are easier and others a bit more forced than we would like. How detailed a status would you like?
For my current situation I don't need any details at all, just: what is the current goal (did it change), is it looking feasible, what are the pain points, is AI helping.

• The current goal is essentially the same as we started with. (If I remember correctly we didn't completely specific exactly which protocols and which security properties and we now have a more precise scope. Similar we the scope of how deep we can go into the dependencies.)
  • Yes, it is looking very feasible. The focus is more on how we can do it best so the code in maintainable, usable, claims are human parse-able, etc.
  • Pain points are rather technical.... let's me think a little more on how to best summarise them.
  • Yes, AI helps a lot for a huge amount of the work.
I am curious on who is reviewing this work as it goes? I have seen very little updates in the Zulip.
I looked over the KVAC stuff this weekend and it looked like it needed an enormous amount of work.

Sam Schlesinger said:

I looked over the KVAC stuff this weekend and it looked like it needed an enormous amount of work.

Yes, indeed. We should find a way to make it clear what we consider to be rather more solid and what is very rough exploration for the moment.

Oliver Butterley said:

  • The current goal is essentially the same as we started with.

Great! What is the current goal? Is there a web page where I can read about the goals and the progress? My understanding of this project is negligible and my first talk is in about 6 hours.

Is anything available other than this https://www.beneficialaifoundation.org/signal-shot ? There has been no update to that page since the announcement of the project, right?

It says "Please create a Zulip account and join this channel to receive updates about Signal Shot." and I did this, but I have not really seen any updates. Where is development taking place? Where do I point people?

I'm sure there was something written somewhere but I'm not sure where. It would be rather useful, particularly since the work is spread across many repos. I'll try to get that sorted. For the moment:

The goal is to verify (key parts of) signal messenger, end-to-end in Lean. All the code we target is written in Rust. The Rust code is translated by a tool to Lean so that theorems about the functional correctness can be proven in Lean and the conclusions will hold for the underlying Rust code. The workflow for the functional correctness task is rather well understood and proceeding steadily. For this task, much of the work is for generally improving the toolchain behind it. Another component of the project is to formalise the protocols used in Lean and prove security properties about them. Here the scope was a bit loose at the beginning but we have now scoped the work rather better, focussing on specific protocols and specific security properties. This part of the work is rather less established and so a lot of this work has been rather exploratory so far. The third part of the project is to add the proofs that the formalised notion of the protocols is faithfully implemented in the real code, building on the functional correctness work.
